analysis.lean: No strong lean: the market is a true pick'em and the model blend is within half a point of it, so pass or wait for injury news.
why: The raw projection (home -2.1, total 221.5) leans Charlotte, but blended with the market at 0.21 weight it is home -0.4 and 219.9, which is basically the market.
Ratings are close and thin: CHA net -0.7 per 100 and WAS -4.5 per 100 after shrinkage, over only 5 games each. The Wizards' defense (113.5 adjusted) is the weakest piece.

Rebounding is the clearest split: CHA offensive rebound rate is 0.329 against WAS defensive 0.328 allowed, while WAS offensive rebounding is only 0.213. Washington's free-throw rate (0.319) offsets some of that.
Both teams are on 1 day of rest, so there is no rest edge. Charlotte won the earlier meeting 110-103, but that is one game.
Total: both sides combine for 221.5 on pace (WAS 104.1, CHA 100.7), but Charlotte's 81-128 and 89-97 losses show how low-scoring it can get. The posted 219.5 looks fair.
risks: Dennis Schroder (foot, questionable, 32.6 min) and Tre Johnson (Achilles, questionable, 22.8 min) both have unclear status. The projection does not appear to count either, because only Champagnie and Dybantsa are listed as already included.
Samples are 5 games per team, so every rating is shaky. Charlotte's results swing from -47 to +12 in one week.
Naz Reid was benched at halftime for discipline reasons, which adds some uncertainty to his minutes.
matchups: WAS defense allows centers +17% points and +10% rebounds per minute against league average, which favors Diabate, Reid and Kalkbrenner inside.
CHA defense allows centers +22% threes and forwards +7% threes, so Washington's bigs and forwards may get open looks from three. WAS takes only 37% of its shots from three.
Charlotte takes 50% of its shots from three, and WAS allows 41%, which is about league average, so there is no clear edge there.
verify: Schroder's status before tip. If he is out, Charlotte's creation and ball security get worse.
Tre Johnson's Achilles status, plus any line move after the injury news.
Whether the Naz Reid discipline issue affects his minutes, and that Knueppel, White and Williams are still out.
Referee crew when it is posted. It is not in the packet.

judgment.why: The market is a pick'em at 219.5, our blend (home -0.4, total 219.9) sits right on it, and I see no concrete edge beyond the two questionable players.

analysis.lean: No strong side or total: the number is efficient, and the only lean is a very slight one toward Chicago +15 because the blended margin is 0.3 short of the line.
why: Blended margin is +14.7 against a -15.0 line, so the model has essentially no edge on the spread.
Blended total is 234.6 against 234.5, which is also no edge. The market fair prices are 0.500 to cover and 0.501 to go over.
Boston is rated +4.2 net per 100 and Chicago -6.4, a gap of about 10.6 points per 100 possessions. Boston won the earlier meeting 134-99.

Chicago allows 0.558 eFG and 130.2 points per game raw, and the matchup shot quality favors Boston (1.139 vs 1.031 expected points/shot, league 1.083). Both samples are only 4-5 games, so the ratings are shrunk toward average.

Chicago starters play 25.1 min in blowouts vs 31.5 in close games (2 and 3 game samples). A big Boston lead could slow the game late and pull the total under, but that sample is too small to move a number.
risks: Samples are 4-5 games per team, so a 15-point spread rests on thin ratings and one 35-point result.
Jalen Smith (left finger sprain) is questionable. The projection already counts him at 70% to play, so his status is not a reason to adjust again.
Large spreads leave a lot of garbage-time variance. Starters resting could swing the cover either way.
matchups: Chicago takes 47% of its shots from three and Boston allows 50% of opponent shots from three (league 42%), so Chicago's volume from deep should be there. Whether those shots go in is uncertain.
Chicago's defense allows +12% forward points and +10% center points per minute vs league, which favors Boston's frontcourt scorers.
verify: Jalen Smith, Tobe Awaka and Patrick Williams status before tip. The injury note for Williams says Out but the text says questionable, so the report is inconsistent.
Whether Boston's rotation is fully healthy. Only Devin Carter (mononucleosis) is listed Out.
The final line and total at tip, since a move toward -15.5 or beyond would change the cover price.

judgment.why: Our blended margin of +14.7 sits almost exactly on the -15.0 line, and the 234.6 total sits on 234.5, so I have no edge beyond the market's fair price.

analysis.lean: No strong lean: the market and our projection agree, so this is a pass or a very small position on LAL at -3.
why: Our ratings project GSW -1.8 and the market-blended number is -2.8, against a market line of GSW +3.0. The gap is under a point.
The blended total of 234.4 matches the posted 234.5, so there is no total edge.
LAL has the better opponent-adjusted net rating (+3.6 vs -0.4 per 100 possessions) and beat GSW 127-105 on 2026-10-21. Both teams are 5 games into the season, so the ratings are tentative.
LAL's shot-quality matchup (1.182 expected points per shot vs 1.098 for GSW, league 1.083) favors the Lakers, but it is a small early sample and is not enough to move the number.
Doncic and Curry are both counted as back in the projection (+2.1 for LAL, +1.6 for GSW), so I did not adjust for them again.
risks: Ziaire Williams (LAL, 28.5 min) is questionable, and Gui Santos (GSW, 24.0 min) is listed doubtful. Both are likely priced in, but a late change would shift the rotations.
Five-game samples are very noisy. GSW's raw last-5 net rating is -1.6, but the stretch includes a 134-114 road win at Denver.
GSW's starters play fewer minutes in blowouts (26.3 vs 30.5 in close games), so a lopsided game can lower the total.
matchups: LAL shoots 45% of its shots from three, and GSW allows 42% (league average). I see no clear edge there.
GSW defense allows centers +9% assists per minute and forwards +6%, which could help Kessler's playmaking. That is a small sample.

analysis.lean: No real edge on the side or the total, so the best play is to pass or stay at the market price.
why: The model has PHX at -0.3 on a neutral rating basis; blended with the market it gives -3.3 for PHX, against a posted line of PHX +4.0. That is within about 1 point of the market, so I make no adjustment.
DEN's opponent-adjusted net is +0.5 per 100 and PHX's is -2.3. That is a small gap, and both are shrunk heavily toward average after 3-4 games.
PHX's raw defense is poor (123.7 allowed per game, opponent eFG 0.568, opponent ORB% 0.362), but that comes from 3 games including an 83-124 loss at POR. The model already uses a shrunk version.

Matchup shot quality favors DEN (1.137 expected points per shot against 1.073 for PHX, league 1.083). DEN's rim-heavy shot mix (30% at the rim, Jokic 120/165 at the rim) meets a PHX defense that allows 32% of shots at the rim.

The total is 231.5 against a projection of 227.2 and a blend of 230.7. Pace is 103.1 for DEN and 102.1 for PHX, but the model's pace is 101.3. The market fair price is 0.498 for the over, which is essentially even.
risks: The injury feed conflicts: Diallo and Cameron Johnson are marked Out, but the notes call both questionable for Friday. Both are minor rotation pieces (22 and 11 minutes).
Oso Ighodaro (PHX, 15 minutes) is questionable, and Mark Williams is out long term after shoulder surgery. That leaves PHX thin at center, and Maluach's rebounding minutes matter against Jokic.
DEN is on 1 day of rest against PHX's 3, and that is a possible fatigue spot. The projection already accounts for rest, so I do not adjust again.
matchups: Jokic against a PHX frontcourt without Williams, and with Ighodaro questionable, could produce rebound and assist volume, since PHX allows centers +6% rebounds per minute.
DEN allows forwards +15% assists per minute, which could help Bridges or Brooks as playmakers, but the sample is small.

judgment.why: The ratings projection (PHX -0.3, total 227.2) is close to the market (PHX +4.0, 231.5), the samples are tiny (DEN 4 games, PHX 3), and I see no concrete edge beyond the market's fair price.

items.t: FanDuel has CHA +1.5 while most books have -0

lessons: Early sample (51 graded picks). Treat every rating as tentative.
Points props are 10-3 with cushion and role signals, but 13 picks is too few to trust. Keep them as normal plays and don't scale them up yet.
Assists, rebounds and threes are 2-10 combined, and rebounds and threes are 0-3 each. Too small to be a rule; lean skip on thin-signal ones.
Picks with no signal are 1-6 and beat the close by -1.6%. Lean skip when no cushion, role, matchup or pace signal backs the pick.
The model said 57.2% overall and 63.5% on 8-12% edges, which went 2-6. Be wary of large edges; don't scale up on size alone.
